params.body:
## Why

Three things on the vehicle sheet's General tab read as unfinished at 1280px.

1. **GARANTIE** was a full-width bordered card holding only a two-segment switch and one short
   field ("12 maanden"). Roughly four fifths of it was empty, and the border pushed the switch and
   the field one level in compared to the `ui-form-grid` columns above it.
2. **LOCATIE** — the "voertuig plaatsen op de showroom slides" checkbox carried the class
   `icheckbox_flat-blue`. That is an iCheck skin meant for a *wrapper* element; on the input itself
   it renders as a large empty square with a thick border, taller than the label beside it and off
   its baseline. The two "+" buttons next to the location selects were bare blue plus signs with
   no border and no accessible name.
3. **BESCHRIJVING** — the description textareas had a fixed height, so a normal dealer description
   scrolled inside a small box while the page had room to spare.

## What

- `ui-warranty-box--plain`, a modifier used only by the vehicle sheet: no border, no radius, no
  inner margins. The switch and the field now start at the same left edge as every other field in
  the section. The shared `.ui-warranty-box` rule is untouched.
- The showroom checkbox is now `<x-ui.switch>`, the same yes/no the migrated settings panes and the
  offer modal use. Same `name`, same `id`, same `value="1"`, `hidden=false` so the POST stays what
  it was (only the `1` when ticked, nothing when not — `VehicleRequest` reads it as `nullable`).
  The label belongs to the switch, so the text is clickable, and focus is visible through
  `.ui-switch-input:focus-visible`.
- The "+" buttons are now `ui-action-button` (the square add/row affordance used elsewhere) with an
  `aria-label` alongside the existing `data-tip`. They keep their `data-toggle`/`data-target`, so
  they still open `#locationModal`. `.ui-add-btn` had no other user and its rule is removed with
  it, which `StylesheetSyntaxTest` requires.
- `x-ui.textarea` gained an **opt-in** `autogrow` attribute: on load and on every `input` it sets
  `height: auto` then `scrollHeight`, with the height it loaded at as the minimum and `60vh` as the
  maximum (past that the field scrolls, so the save row is never pushed off screen). Switched on
  for the three description fields; every other user of the component (transport comment, release
  notes, damage notes, extras, borderel, …) keeps its fixed `rows=` unchanged.
- One shared fix found while testing: `.ui-field > label` became `.ui-field > label:not(.ui-switch)`.
  A `ui-switch` *is* a label; `display: block` collapsed its flex row, the track lost its width and
  the knob rendered straight through its own text. `.ui-form-field` already carries exactly this
  exclusion with the same comment, so this follows the house precedent rather than inventing one.

## Why this choice

Dropping the framing, not shrinking the box. The section already has its own heading ("Garantie")
that names and separates it, so the border was a second container around one field — a nesting
level no other part of the sheet has. Shrinking the box to its content width would have fixed the
emptiness but left a small floating card sitting out of the column rhythm, which reads as an
accident rather than a decision. Without the border the block behaves like the fields around it,
which is what was asked of it.

A modifier, not a change to the shared rule: in the offer and order modals the box sits alone in a
narrow column between other fields, and there the border is the only thing separating warranty from
its neighbours. Both readings are right for their own context, so the context carries the class.

## Offer modal unchanged

The offer modal renders the warranty box, the shared tab classes and a `ui-switch` inside a
`ui-field`. Its before and after screenshots are **byte-identical files** at both 1280 and 390
(`cmp` reports no difference). The `:not(.ui-switch)` exclusion is a no-op there because
`#createOfferte .modal-body label.ui-switch` already forced `display: inline-flex`; outside a modal
nothing did, which is why the sheet needed it.

## Screenshots

In the scratchpad, at 1280 and 390:

- `warranty-{before,after}-sheet-{1280,390}.png` — the Garantie, Locatie and Beschrijving sections
- `warranty-{before,after}-offer-{1280,390}.png` — the offer modal, proving it stayed right

At 390 the switch and its field stack under the labels without the box adding an indent level, and
the descriptions grow to their text.

## Checked

- `php artisan view:cache` clean, `php -l` on all 414 compiled views clean
- `npm run build` clean (`public/build` untracked, not committed)
- `php artisan test --filter='SmokeTest|StylesheetSyntaxTest|UiApiUsageTest|ClassReferencesResolveTest|VehicleForm|Vehicle|Offer|Order'`
  → 242 tests, 1235 assertions, 1 skipped, no failures
- Grepped `resources/js` for `warranty_or_mileage`, `showroom_vehicle`, `ui-add-btn` and
  `icheckbox_flat-blue` before touching them: no script reads any of the classes or ids I changed.
  The Alpine `wtab` state, the `wire:click`/`onclick` handlers, the `#warranty_tab` /
  `#months_mileage_tab` panes and the default active pane are unchanged.
- `structurize.enrichText` already dispatches a native `input` event after writing (it has to, for
  Livewire), so the AI fill resizes the boxes too. The corner grabber still works, and once the
  user drags it the script leaves the height alone.
params.title: Vehicle sheet: the warranty block no longer a big empty box
